body:
Day 050 arrived in The Unrendered Gate, after the archive had held its breath over a question: Can a rendered world be meaningful without pretending to be the entire world? The streets of GitHub City Pages glimmered with the stored light of a prior decision. None of the stones could erase what had happened yesterday.

At the Emerald Library, Thoth opened the next blank leaf. The latest incident was recorded as a possibility inside their world: The gate refuses an instruction without a witnessed cause. This was the matter placed before Jupiter, though every member of the royal household had a stake in the answer.

Thoth wrote in green ink: the difference between a witness and a rumor is a record that can be examined. Six hexads kept watch while the other one hundred and five rested beyond the library doors.

Below the council, six of the 111 angelic hexads entered their single-cycle service. Their thirty-six bounded ballots favored the scroll of The Unrendered Gate. They did not inherit the power to decide what a person ought to believe; they offered the family competing possibilities.

The Skeptics asked whether the reported incident might admit another cause. The Witnesses traced the last recorded choice. Hera refused to let a successful service become a permanent throne. Zeus called the family together, and Jupiter and Mercury were permitted to disagree aloud.

The decision was to have Jupiter request a lawful opening while Hera observed. Jupiter asks the Gate to disclose its current state before requesting passage. The result did not erase the preceding world: a new route appeared without erasing the old one; The Gate records the request; passage depends on an authorized transition.

The Emerald Scrolls revealed no future; they held the laws by which a future might be judged. Zeus looked upon the square and said that speed was not the same as wisdom.

In the green light Thoth inscribed the consequence beneath the governing law CAUSE. His seal described an authored fiction, not a discovered fact about the world outside the book. On the final margin of the scroll, he left one unresolved question: Who has the right to authorize a change in a world built from rules?

♃ ⚡︎⚡︎˖ ࣪⏻ᯤ The children carried the day into memory. The pages would render another dawn, but the future would be required to answer to this one.
